sources: The Wall Street Journal, 'America's Gulf Allies Prepare for New Round of Strikes on Iran -- and the Blowback' ( dateline); Saturday Trump-Netanyahu call details earlier reported by Axios
fault_line: Strike now to finish it vs diplomacy first -- and who pays: Gulf states fear they absorb Iran's retaliation while the US decides. Social fault line: war-for-political-survival accusations vs deterrence; pocketbook angle

sections.what_happened: Gulf allies are steeling themselves for a heavy US bombardment of Iran that could trigger retaliation against their own economic and civilian infrastructure as early as this week. Trump has been leaning toward a large post-election attack targeting Iranian infrastructure and nuclear sites but has not decided. On Saturday's call he told Netanyahu he wanted to give diplomacy a chance first; Netanyahu pressed for strikes immediately after the midterms; Israel's military has attack plans ready and is on high alert. Qatar-mediated talks are stuck on sequencing -- whether the US or Iran concedes first. Trump Iowa rally quote: 'The only reason why I'm not finished with Iran is I want to be nice... But at some point we're going to have to give them the hammer.'
sections.what_verified: WSJ (people familiar with the call; mediators) + Axios (earlier Saturday-call details) converge on the call's shape; Trump 'No' on post-midterm strikes (0300-01) and Vance 'progress, no deadlines' (0200-02) are the on-record counterweight -- Trump has NOT decided
sections.what_disputed: Trump on record Nov 2 (Reuters via 0300-01): asked if considering striking Iran after the midterms, answered 'No'; Vance: progress in indirect talks, no deadlines set. WSJ itself says Trump 'hasn't decided' and 'leaning toward' -- not a decision. Gulf-allies bracing is WSJ single-source reporting (unnamed people familiar), not an official Gulf statement.
sections.why_matters: Claim-bust / endgame frame: 'Trump said NO -- but his allies are bracing for war THIS WEEK.' Hard number in title (Gulf bracing; hammer quote). Lead with the on-record 'No' vs the WSJ 'leaning toward' tension, not with the strike as fact.
